lines.text: It is two in the morning, and you are on call. An agent needs a risky command approved.
Normally only one person can answer. If your phone is silent, the agent and the outage both wait.
Each workspace has its own private Slack channel, and the approval request lands right there.
Any teammate in that channel can approve or deny. It no longer depends on one person.
Sam wakes up and reads the exact command, not a vague summary.
Sam taps allow once. That covers this single command only.
The agent carries on. The restart goes out, and the service recovers.
Agent R Q records who clicked. Approved by Sam, at seven minutes past two. No shared login.
Denying is just as easy. Maya denied a delete command, and her name is on it too.
The team shares the load, so nobody carries every alert alone.
In the morning, the log tells the story. What was asked, who answered, and when.
Share the on call load, and keep a signed trail. Try it at Agent R Q dot com.
